requirements: Build a 3D Unity survival game set in a compact urban arena.
The player can move, aim, and use a ranged weapon against incoming enemies.
Enemies arrive in increasingly difficult waves and pursue the player.
Track player health, ammunition, current wave, and score in the user interface.
The run ends when the player's health reaches zero.

tasks.description: Create the Unity 3D project and organize the initial folders and packages.
Build a compact urban arena with a ground plane, cover, buildings, lighting, and a player spawn point.
Create placeholder player and enemy objects and configure the scene layers and physics.
Implement third-person player movement and camera aiming.
Add player health and a clear damage and death state.
Add a basic ranged weapon with firing, ammunition, and reload behavior.
Create an enemy that can take damage, pursue the player, and attack at close range.
Create a wave manager that spawns enemies and increases wave difficulty over time.
Award score when enemies are defeated and detect when a wave is cleared.
Display player health, ammunition, wave number, and score in the HUD.
Add start, pause, and game-over screens with a restart option.
Assemble existing gameplay systems into a minimal playable SampleScene and verify a PlayMode smoke test.
Play through multiple waves and tune enemy counts, damage, and ammunition balance.

assumptions: The first version uses placeholder or free assets rather than custom art.
The game is a single-player, offline experience for desktop.
The first playable version uses one arena and one enemy type.
The camera is third-person and the weapon uses a simple hitscan or projectile implementation.
